source: S22 SEL-751 Instruction Manual date code 20260910, Appendix A firmware revision history (FID String / Summary of Revisions table). Extracted by A2 with pdftotext; lineage taken from each row's 'Includes all the functions of' clause.
rule_applied: A1 (ADR-0005 6d82243): collect only from allowlisted FIDs that carry every communications-restart fix. Appendix A records each fix only on the branches where SEL shipped it, and never says whether other branches had the defect. Each branch's first release (V0) has no 'Includes' clause, so inheritance across branches is not documented. Treating a fix as inherited by a branch whose V0 is dated after the fix is an INFERENCE, marked as such. It needs SEL confirmation before it counts as documented.
fid_match: Match the full FID string: SEL-751-R<branch>-V<n>-Z<...>-D<date>, with V >= min_version on an allowed branch and the Z and D fields equal to an Appendix A row. Any FID not in Appendix A (later releases, special builds, SEL-751A) is unknown and fails closed.

F1.what: certain Ethernet traffic could cause diagnostic restarts

F2.what: rare issue where Telnet traffic could cause a diagnostic restart

F3.what: deliberately crafted Ethernet traffic could cause a diagnostic restart

F4.what: BPDU packet of invalid size could cause a diagnostic restart

F5.what: accessing the relay via communications ports (among other operations) could cause a diagnostic restart

F6.what: Ethernet port could lock up in switched mode under heavy network traffic

F7.what: denial-of-service condition in the web server could trigger diagnostic restarts

F8.what: maliciously crafted CID file could cause the relay to disable (needs a file write, which the collector never does)
